nodes.name: NF Cleaning
nodes.procedure: The NF (2×3 cm²) was sonicated sequentially in acetone, 3 M HCl, and DI water for 10 min each.
nodes.source_text: The cleaned NF (2×3 cm²) was sonicated sequentially in acetone, 3 M HCl, and DI water for 10 min each.

nodes.name: Hydrothermal Synthesis of pre-CoMoO
nodes.procedure: 0.30 mmol of (NH4)6Mo7O24·4H2O and 0.12 mmol of Co(NO3)2·6H2O were dissolved in 30 mL of DI water. Then, 50 μL of HCl was added to adjust the pH. After stirring at room temperature for 30 min, the cleaned NF was immersed in the solution and transferred to a 50 mL Teflon-lined autoclave. The autoclave was heated at 150°C for 5 h. After cooling to room temperature, the resulting product was washed thoroughly with DI water and ethanol, then dried under vacuum at 60°C overnight to yield pre-CoMoO.

nodes.name: Phosphidation to CoMoO-P
nodes.procedure: The dried pre-CoMoO (2×3 cm²) and 1.0 g of NaH2PO2·H2O were placed separately in ceramic boats with pre-CoMoO at the center and NaH2PO2·H2O upstream in a quartz tube furnace. The furnace was heated to 400°C at 10°C min⁻¹ under N₂ atmosphere and maintained for 2 h. After natural cooling, CoMoO-P was collected.
nodes.source_text: For phosphidation, the dried pre-CoMoO (2×3 cm²) and 1.0 g of NaH2PO2·H2O were placed separately in ceramic boats... the CoMoO-P sample was collected.

nodes.name: Thermal Treatment
nodes.procedure: pre-CoMoO was thermally treated under the same thermal conditions as CoMoO-P without NaH2PO2·H2O to obtain CoMoO-HT.
nodes.source_text: Meanwhile, pre-CoMoO was thermally treated under the same thermal conditions as CoMoO-P without NaH2PO2·H2O to obtain CoMoO-HT.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS element mappings reveal homogeneous distribution of Co, Mo, O, and P elements in CoMoO-P, confirming successful P incorporation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) element mappings of CoMoO-P (Fig. 1a) reveal the homogeneous distribution of Co, Mo, O, and P elements, confirming successful P incorporation.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show all three samples (pre-CoMoO, CoMoO-P, CoMoO-HT) are nanoplates on nickel foam; CoMoO-P and CoMoO-HT have uniform nanoplates ~100 nm thick.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscope (SEM) images (Figs. 1b-d) show that all three samples are nanoplates on the nickel foams.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns show pre-CoMoO comprises mixed hydrated cobalt molybdate phases, CoMoO-P transforms into P-incorporated β-CoMoO4 with poor crystallinity, CoMoO-HT shows mixture of β-CoMoO4 and α-CoMoO4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns (Fig. 1e) show that pre-CoMoO comprises mixed hydrated cobalt molybdate phases...

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM images of CoMoO-P reveal interplanar spacing of 4.65 Å corresponding to (201) plane of β-CoMoO4 with abundant lattice defects, vacancies, dislocations, and distortions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution transmission electron microscope (HRTEM) images of CoMoO-P (Figs. 2f&g) reveal an interplanar spacing of 4.65 Å... In addition, abundant lattice defects, such as vacancies, dislocations, and distortions, are observed (Fig. 1g).

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern of CoMoO-P confirms (201) and (222) planes of β-CoMoO4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern (Fig. 1h) further confirms the (201) and (222) planes of β-CoMoO4.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms P-incorporation in CoMoO-P with P 2p peaks at 134.6 eV (P-O), 130.4 eV and 129.6 eV (M-P); Co 2p peaks shift ~1.0 eV higher in CoMoO-P; Mo 3d shows Mo6+, Mo5+, Mo4+ states; O 1s shows prominent oxygen vacancies at 531.9 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) elucidates surface composition and chemical states.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-tested EDS analysis shows after-CoMoO-P exhibits less Mo loss (13.9%) than after-CoMoO-HT (86.9%) and after-pre-CoMoO (97.2%).
nodes.evidence_snippet: EDS analysis of the post-tested CoMoO-P (denoted as after-CoMoO-P) reveals pronounced differences among the three samples (Figs. 3a&S15).

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-test XRD shows after-CoMoO-P retains β-CoMoO4 with newly formed α-CoMoO4 and Co(OH)2; after-CoMoO-HT shows complete transition to α-CoMoO4 and Co(OH)2; after-pre-CoMoO transforms entirely to Co(OH)2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XRD patterns (Fig. 3e) indicate phase evolution in all samples.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-test HRTEM of after-CoMoO-P reveals hierarchical structure: β-CoMoO4 core (3.07 Å, 310 plane), α-CoMoO4 intermediate (2.497 Å, 131 plane), Co(OH)2 shell (1.506 Å, 111 plane).
nodes.evidence_snippet: HRTEM analysis of after-CoMoO-P (Figs. 3f&g) reveals a hierarchical structure composed of β-CoMoO4, α-CoMoO4, and Co(OH)2. The central β-CoMoO4 phase displays a lattice fringe of 3.07 Å, indexed to the (310) plane.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-test SAED of after-CoMoO-P exhibits sharp diffraction spots confirming local ordered multiphase polycrystalline structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: SAED pattern (Fig. 3h) exhibits sharp diffraction spots confirming a local ordered multiphase polycrystalline structure...

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-test XPS Co 2p shows dominant Co2+ signals confirming Co(OH)2 formation in all samples; after-CoMoO-P Mo 3d shows predominantly Mo6+ peaks with weak signals in after-CoMoO-HT and undetectable in after-pre-CoMoO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XPS Co 2p spectra (Fig. 3i) show dominant Co2+ signals in all postcatalysts, confirming the formation of Co(OH)2. In the Mo 3d spectra (Fig. 3j), after-CoMoO-P shows predominantly Mo6+ peaks...

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS results validate reduced Mo leaching in CoMoO-P with only 8.2% Mo loss after extended stability testing, compared to 97.2% for after-pre-CoMoO and 86.9% for after-CoMoO-HT.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometry (ICP-MS) results (Fig. S20, Table S3) further validate the reduced Mo leaching in CoMoO-P... Quantitative EDS analysis (Fig. S19) shows a Mo loss of 97.2% for after-pre-CoMoO, 86.9% for after-CoMoO-HT, and only 13.9% for after-CoMoO-P.

nodes.characterization_summary: In-situ Raman of CoMoO-P shows evolution from Co-O-Mo bands (826-958 cm⁻¹) to intensified Co(OH)2 peaks at 504 cm⁻¹ with potential, indicating Mo leaching and redeposition.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In-situ Raman spectroscopy (Figs. 4a-c) was combined with ICP-MS concentration profiles...

nodes.characterization_summary: In-situ ATR-FTIR shows CoMoO-P peaks at 3743 cm⁻¹ (weakly adsorbed water/OH) and 3647 cm⁻¹ (strongly H-bonded OH*) increase significantly with negative potential.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In-situ attenuated total reflectance Fourier-transform Infrared (ATR-FTIR) spectra provide additional insight into water and hydroxyl adsorption behavior...
